title: DAG Cycle Spotter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: DGX Evaluation for Textbook Generation
description: Inspect six small prerequisite graphs, decide which contain a cycle, and mark the concepts that lie on it.

educational.topic: Learning Graphs, MicroSims, and Content Generation Rules
learningObjectives: The learner will distinguish prerequisite graphs that contain a cycle from graphs that do not, in 6 small graphs, with at least 5 of 6 classified correctly.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit an answer, then see the correct answer and the reason
keyQuestions: Graph 4 has a concept that is not on the cycle. Explain why removing that concept would not make the graph valid.
commonMisconceptions: Two concepts that share a prerequisite form a cycle.
A graph with two disconnected parts is invalid.
A concept that depends on itself is not a cycle.
A longer chain of dependencies is more likely to contain a cycle.

chapter_title: Learning Graphs, MicroSims, and Content Generation Rules
